notes.title: Things Too Ugly Art Book & Soundtrack Available Now
notes.notes:
Hello Friends,

Thank you for following along with Things Too Ugly. It’s been wonderful experiencing your support and engagement. I hope you’ve enjoyed the story and world building of the game, but should you have lingering questions, a longing to look beyond your office, or simply a want for more, I’ve got some good news: I’ve been hard at work on some extra content, and it’s now available.

The Art & World of Things Too Ugly

Explore this digital art book companion that takes the form of the fictional Cryptogram Magazine, a publication dedicated to the strange and scientific in the rural midwestern United States. 30 two-page spreads! Within, you will find a collection of stories ranging from cryptid sightings to emerging technologies, as well as an exciting exposé on Terebro Inc. following the events of the game. Pore over photographs, drawings, and digital collages. Dozens of pages of concept art, writing, and more comprise this special Cryptogram issue.

The Sounds of Things Too Ugly

Listen to the eclectic and haunting original soundtrack. Revisit the sounds of Father Floodplain & the Midnight Communion, It Came from the Aether, and more (even if you haven’t found them on the in-game radio).

Again, I thank you for your support, and I hope you’ll enjoy delving further into the world of Things Too Ugly.

Working hard, working safely, working always.

-Kevin, Professor Space Games

notes.title: It's Time to Clock In – Things Too Ugly is Out Now!
notes.notes:
Things Too Ugly is officially live on Steam! Step into the dimly lit office of a Risk Assessment Data Processor, where every document, diagram, and cryptic puzzle could be the key unlocking a long-buried truth—or something far worse.

Your task is simple: protect the company’s legacy. But as you piece together fragments of the past, the unease builds. What will you choose to reveal?

Thank you for being part of this journey—your support, wishlists, and feedback have made this possible. If you come across something strange, share your discoveries in the community forums—but please keep spoilers marked, so everyone can experience the mystery for themselves.

Good luck

notes.title: The Night Shift Begins January 16th, 2025
notes.notes:
Dear Friends and Future Players,

The moment we’ve all been waiting for is finally here! We are overjoyed to share that Things Too Ugly, the first-person narrative puzzle game from Professor Space Games, will officially launch on January 16th, 2025. Soon, you will be able to peep the shadows of Terebro Inc., a corporation hiding long-buried secrets. 

We are incredibly grateful for your anticipation and support. As we count down to launch day, we encourage you to share your excitement with the world! 

Thank you for being part of this journey with us,
The Professor Space Games & Baltoro Games

notes.title: The Demo Has Done Its Job
notes.notes:
Risk Assessors,

The night shift is far from over, but the tools you’ve been using are... out of date. As we approach the final stages of development, we’ve decided to take the demo offline, as the current version no longer reflects the updates and enhancements we've made to the full game.

Since Things Too Ugly is a single-sitting story best experienced as a complete package, we decided taking off the demo would be the best course of action. But don’t fret, the release date will be revealed soon. We can’t wait for you to unravel the mysteries of Terebro Inc. 

Thank you for your enthusiasm and support for Things Too Ugly! Your feedback on the Steam demo has been instrumental in helping us refine the game.

Stay vigilant.

notes.title: "Things Too Ugly" Demo Update
notes.notes:
I’m excited to share that the demo of Things Too Ugly has received an update. 
The demo plunges players into the night shift in a new job as they commence a thrilling sci-fi mystery, 
and it has been  e x p a n d e d  to provide them with a little more:

+ Players can progress the story further
+ A DEMO-EXCLUSIVE EASTER EGG PUZZLE has been added
	
I want to thank all who have played the Things Too Ugly demo. It’s been a blast to watch people engage with the game’s mechanics, story, and puzzles.

If you have not yet played the demo, I encourage you to take a look and kick-off the mystery within. If you have already begun the story, I invite you to return for more.

Things Too Ugly has been a labor of love, and I am so thrilled to be able to share it with you all.

Happy gaming!

-Kevin, Professor Space Games
